correctness.rationale: The eight-ballot score differences give the stated covariance, full lattice and zero step. Scaling Fourier inversion of the pinned marginal gives pair masses 2/(pi n) and sqrt(2/(pi(p^2+q^2)n)) and a centered nondegenerate conditional gap. Thus half of tied pairs beat the third at leading order, and the full-lattice triple events have orders at most n^-2 and n^-1. Read the proof's pair-count discussion as counting strict winners once and then adding the triple probability once, or counting weak pair ties and subtracting two triple probabilities. The finite assertion follows from (U,V)=(kp,-kq) and |V|<=n, and q=1 makes n<q vacuous for n>=1. This is a pair equality statement only. Exact ordered-profile replay through four voters (python3 /workspace/replay_thiele.py) confirms score differences, covariance, exact pair identity and winning-tie examples.

The additional n<q clause is not itself stated in record 1, but is an immediate coprimality-and-range corollary of its explicit integer score-difference expression and does not establish a distinct substantive tie asymptotic. In fact |U|+|V|<=n from the mutually exclusive ballot contributions, so the same argument gives the stronger n<p+q cutoff; the frozen bound is not sharp in general.
